paper_metadata.title: Accelerated quantum Monte Carlo with mitigated error on noisy quantum computer

experiments.description: Theoretical QCMC framework for real-time quantum many-body simulation using second-order Pauli-operator-expansion (POE) and leading-order-rotation (LOR) summation formulas, with compact and forward-backward circuits and error mitigation analysis.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-circuit Monte Carlo (QCMC) with second-order POE and LOR summation formulas

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum many-body Hamiltonian terms are represented as Pauli operators on n qubits; samples s index unitary-circuit terms in the summation formula.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate transition amplitude <psi_f|e^{iHt*} O e^{-iHt}|psi_i> by Monte Carlo over circuit terms.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on |0>^n in the forward-backward circuit; probabilistic error cancellation for noisy gates.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_j h_j sigma_j, with sigma_j in {I,X,Y,Z}^{⊗n}

problem_instance.description: General theoretical many-body real-time evolution; no single fixed benchmark instance for the main framework.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivations plus numerical demonstrations on small model systems; variance and sign-problem behavior analyzed theoretically.

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Proportional to N; compact circuit depth matches Lie-Trotter-Suzuki product depth plus controlled-correction gates; forward-backward circuit depth is doubled relative to compact circuit.
quantum_resources.cnot_count: At most n controlled-NOTs per controlled-correction gate on all-to-all network for POE; up to 4n for LOR on all-to-all; up to 4n-3 for POE and 8n-4 for LOR on linear network.
quantum_resources.num_shots: 2M_tot total circuit shots in the variance analysis; Ms shots per circuit in the general protocol, with optimal Ms = 1 for unbiased estimation.

noise_model.mitigation_details: Probabilistic error cancellation using quasi-probability decomposition; forward-backward circuit with postselection; tomography purification of ancilla qubit.
noise_model.noise_description: Pauli depolarizing error model for controlled-NOT gates; probabilistic error cancellation; inherent error mitigation via postselection/tomography

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Sample generation of circuit terms s on the classical computer according to P(s); compute theta_s; compose circuits.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average measured real and imaginary parts; multiply by C_A^{2N}; optionally apply postselection formula or error-mitigation reweighting.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing_details: Estimate <psi_f|e^{iHt} O e^{-iHt}|psi_i> from empirical mean of circuit outcomes.

results.value: factor of approximately 4 × 10^4 reduction in required sample number
factor of approximately 4 × 10^6 reduction in required sample number
at most n per controlled-correction gate on all-to-all network for POE; up to 4n for LOR on all-to-all; up to 4n-3 for POE and 8n-4 for LOR on linear network
O(Δt^5) for fourth-order product formula comparison
C_A = 1 + O(Δt^3) for second-order POE; C_A = sqrt(1 + C_L^2 + C_T) for second-order LOR

experiments.description: Numerical demonstration of inherent error mitigation for the one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model using the first-order summation formula and forward-backward circuit with postselection/tomography.

algorithm.variant: QCMC on the 1D Fermi-Hubbard model with first-order LOR/POE-derived summation formula and forward-backward circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Fermi-Hubbard model encoded into 2N_L qubits via Jordan-Wigner transformation; N_L = 3 sites.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Postselection on all system qubits being |0>^n in the forward-backward circuit; tomography purification of ancilla qubit.

dataset_specification.description: NL = 3 sites; spinful fermions; Jordan-Wigner encoded into 6 qubits.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noisy quantum computing simulated classically; compare raw, postselection, purification, and exact/Trotter results as a function of time.

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Forward-backward circuit depth with doubled S1 and S1' products relative to compact circuit; at most 85 time steps in the simulation.
quantum_resources.cnot_count: 14 controlled-NOT gates per S1; total controlled-NOT count above 2380 at 85 time steps.

noise_model.mitigation_details: Forward-backward circuit with postselection; tomography purification; comparison against raw noisy data and exact/Trotter baselines.
noise_model.noise_description: Depolarizing Pauli noise on controlled-NOT gates; single-qubit gates, initialization, and measurement neglected in the numerical simulation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical simulation of noisy quantum circuits; construct Jordan-Wigner encoded Hamiltonian and summation-formula coefficients.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute observable from postselected/tomographically purified ancilla measurements and compare with exact and Trotter results.

classical_baselines.method_name: Lie-Trotter-Suzuki product formula without machine errors
classical_baselines.value: exact/Trotter baseline used for comparison; no numeric value stated
shown in figure; no exact numeric value stated in text

speedup_claims.factor: error mitigation makes overall accuracy higher than product formula without machine errors
speedup_claims.baseline_method: Lie-Trotter-Suzuki product formula without machine errors
speedup_claims.conditions: numerical simulation of 1D Fermi-Hubbard model with p = 0.03% per CNOT, Ns = 10000, up to 85 time steps
speedup_claims.caveats: Comparison is based on classical simulation of noisy circuits, not hardware execution.

scalability_data.metric_value: 14 per S1; above 2380 total at 85 time steps

experiments.description: Numerical comparison of sign-problem severity and observable estimation for the Fermi-Hubbard model using classical Monte Carlo (zeroth-order POE) versus quantum-circuit Monte Carlo (first-order LOR).

algorithm.variant: QCMC versus classical QMC comparison on the Fermi-Hubbard model

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate <O> = <psi_i|e^{iHt} O e^{-iHt}|psi_i> and monitor phase average <e^{i theta_q}>.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Fermi-Hubbard Hamiltonian in Eq. (74) / Appendix B Jordan-Wigner form.

problem_instance.description: Three-site Fermi-Hubbard chain used to compare sign-problem behavior between classical and quantum-circuit Monte Carlo.

dataset_specification.description: 3-site chain, J = 2, U = 4, initial state c^†_{1,↑} c^†_{2,↓} c^†_{3,↑}|Vac>.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Phase average and observable plotted versus time; QCMC and classical Monte Carlo both evaluated on a classical computer for the small system.

quantum_resources.circuit_depth: First-order LOR circuit depth corresponding to one S1 product per time step; exact depth not numerically specified.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate samples from the suboptimal distribution in Eq. (10) and evaluate circuit amplitudes.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute phase average <e^{i theta_q}> and observable expectation values from sampled amplitudes.
